hints.title: 2 x N Grid Tile Interlocking Obstacle
hints.text: Tiling a 2 x n board with 2x1 dominoes and L-trominoes produces states where rows can be completely covered or partially extended. How can deriving the recurrence between full and partial board coverages calculate tilings modulo 10^9 + 7?

hints.title: Tiling Linear Recurrence Invariant
hints.text: For n >= 3, the number of tilings satisfies f(n) = 2 * f(n - 1) + f(n - 3) modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Four-State Rolling Progression Procedure
hints.text: Handle small n directly: 1 for n=1, 2 for n=2, 5 for n=3. For larger n, maintain three rolling variables representing f(n-1), f(n-2), and f(n-3). In each step from 4 to n, compute (2 * f(n-1) + f(n-3)) % (10^9 + 7) and slide the registers. Return the latest value.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of 2 x N board (up to 1000)
complexity.notes: Iterates N times with three rolling state integers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating tile placement trees causes exponential state explosion.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant scalar variables eliminate table allocations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Deriving the simplified recurrence f(n) = 2 * f(n - 1) + f(n - 3) from interlocking tromino geometries.
